userStories.title: Unattended ACP profile, skills delivery and a public runSubagent
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the unattended ACP posture and skills delivery while exposing the existing one-turn subagent API.

**Motivation** — koda's runner can launch `nax plan`, `nax run`, `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix`, but it cannot run "the spec reviewer on this spec" as a job, and the koda flow needs exactly that.

**Approach** — `acpSubagentProfile` (`packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-subagent-profile.ts`) derives an ACP subagent's profile from its agent file. In chat, an agent with no `tools:` line inherits the chat's own profile (`ask` in guarded, `full` in full). Unattended, nobody can answer an ask, so an agent with no `tools:` line opens read-only on `review` instead. An agent that declares a write tool still gets the chat's own profile, and the operator override `agent.acpSubagents.profile` still wins over everything. The derivation order becomes:

1. `override` set: return it.
2. `tools` declared and naming a write tool: the chat's own profile for `mode`.
3. `tools` undefined and `unattended` not true: the chat's own profile for `mode`.
4. Otherwise: `review`.

So a read-only `review` subagent on `cursor`, which enforces no read-only itself, still refuses to start through the existing `readOnlyRefusal` path; under `nax agents run` that refusal is status `failed`.

**Skills for an unattended ACP agent.** An ACP subagent is handed only the providers in `ACP_SUBAGENT_PROVIDER_IDS` (`["nax-workflow", "nax-memory"]`, `acp-subagent-session.ts`). The skill message `buildSkillInvocationMessage` builds tells the model to load the skill's references with `nax-skills__load`, and an ACP agent's own Read may not reach `~/.claude` from its sandbox. So when `unattended` is true, the ACP subagent is also handed the `nax-skills` provider (still filtered by the agent's `tools:` list as the other providers are). Chat ACP subagents, where `unattended` is absent, are unchanged.

`RunSubagentInput` in `packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-session.ts`. Target: gains `readonly unattended?: true`, which the private `subagentProfile` passes to `acpSubagentProfile`.

`deliveredProviders` in `packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-subagent-session.ts`. Target: when `input.unattended` is true, a provider whose id is `nax-skills` is delivered as well as those in `ACP_SUBAGENT_PROVIDER_IDS`, under the same `tools:` filter. `runSubagent` and `RunSubagentInput`/`RunSubagentResult` become exports of the `@/chat` barrel (they are not today).

ACs 3 to 7 are regression pins over the unchanged branches; the others fail first. Extend the three existing ACP test files listed in the analysis, preserving their current cases.

**Scope** — In: profile derivation, flag propagation, conditional provider delivery, chat barrel exports. Out: headless execution/asks/CLI orchestration (US-003/004/008/009). Delivering `nax-skills` to chat ACP subagents; only unattended runs get it. Translating an agent file's `tools:` list into ACP tool restrictions beyond read-only versus not is unchanged from part (a).

**Interface** —
```typescript
acpSubagentProfile(input: { tools: readonly string[] | undefined; mode: ChatMode; override?: AcpSubagentProfile; unattended?: true }): AcpSubagentProfile
```
`RunSubagentInput` gains `readonly unattended?: true`; export `runSubagent`, `RunSubagentInput` and `RunSubagentResult` from `@/chat`.

[unit] acpSubagentProfile({ tools: undefined, mode: "full", unattended: true }) returns "review".
[unit] acpSubagentProfile({ tools: ["Read", "Write"], mode: "guarded", unattended: true }) returns "ask".
[unit] acpSubagentProfile({ tools: ["Read", "Edit"], mode: "full", unattended: true }) returns "full".
[unit] acpSubagentProfile({ tools: ["Read", "Grep"], mode: "guarded", unattended: true }) returns "review".
[unit] acpSubagentProfile({ tools: undefined, mode: "guarded", override: "full", unattended: true }) returns "full".
[unit] acpSubagentProfile({ tools: undefined, mode: "guarded" }) with no unattended field returns "ask".

[unit] runSubagent with model acp:claude, an agent whose tools is undefined, mode guarded and unattended: true, with _subagentSessionDeps.createAgentSession stubbed, passes options whose profile is "review" to createAgentSession.

[unit] runSubagent with model acp:cursor, an agent whose tools is undefined and unattended: true returns isError: true with content starting [chat] subagent <qualifiedName> could not start read-only:, and _subagentSessionDeps.createAgentSession is never called.

When an unattended ACP input has allowedTools ["nax-skills__*"], chatAcpTools receives nax-skills and not nax-workflow.

add `unattended?: true` to `RunSubagentInput` and pass it from `subagentProfile` to `acpSubagentProfile`.
deliver the `nax-skills` provider as well when `input.unattended` is true.
add the `unattended` cases beside the existing derivation cases; existing cases keep passing unchanged, since `unattended` is optional and absent in them.
add the two `nax-skills` delivery cases; existing cases keep passing unchanged, since none sets `unattended`.
add the two `unattended: true` runSubagent cases; existing cases keep passing unchanged.

userStories.title: Task input and skill expansion
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve one task source and expand only leading skill invocations with the shared chat builder.

**Motivation** — koda's runner can launch `nax plan`, `nax run`, `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix`, but it cannot run "the spec reviewer on this spec" as a job, and the koda flow needs exactly that.

**Approach** — Exactly one of `--task` and `--task-file` is required. `--task-file` is read as UTF-8 text with `Bun.file(path).text()`; a relative path resolves against `--dir`.

A task whose trimmed text begins with `/` followed by a name of one or more characters from `[A-Za-z0-9:_.-]`, then whitespace or the end of the text, is a skill invocation. The name is looked up with `catalog.findSkill(name)`; the rest of the text after the name, trimmed, is the arguments. The task sent to the agent is `buildSkillInvocationMessage({ skill, args })` from `@/prompts`, the call the chat slash command makes in `catalogCommand` (`packages/nax/src/tui/chat/slash-commands.ts`). A name with no skill is a usage error. Catalog commands (`findCommand`) are not expanded. A task that does not match the pattern is sent unchanged.

`packages/nax/src/cli/agents-run-task.ts`: `resolveAgentsRunTask(input: { task?: string; taskFile?: string; cwd: string; catalog: Pick<ResourceCatalog, "findSkill"> }, deps?: { readText: (path: string) => Promise<string> }): Promise<string>`, returning the message to send, and throwing `NaxError` code `AGENTS_RUN_USAGE` for a usage error. The default `readText` is `(path) => Bun.file(path).text()`.

Failure handling: neither or both task sources -> `pass exactly one of --task or --task-file`; unreadable file -> `cannot read task file <path>: <reason>`; empty text after trimming -> `the task is empty`; unknown skill -> `skill <name> not found`. All are AGENTS_RUN_USAGE errors; file errors preserve the CLI-supplied path in the message.

**Scope** — In: source selection, injected/default reader, empty-task validation and skill-only expansion. Out: trust/config checks (US-008), model resolution (US-006), agent execution (US-003). Catalog commands (`findCommand` templates, including their `` !`cmd` `` shell lines) are not expanded in `--task`; only skills are.

**Interface** —
```typescript
resolveAgentsRunTask(input: { task?: string; taskFile?: string; cwd: string; catalog: Pick<ResourceCatalog, "findSkill"> }, deps?: { readText: (path: string) => Promise<string> }): Promise<string>
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] resolveAgentsRunTask({ task: "review the spec", cwd, catalog }) resolves to "review the spec".
[unit] resolveAgentsRunTask with neither task nor taskFile rejects with a NaxError whose code is AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and whose message is pass exactly one of --task or --task-file.
[unit] resolveAgentsRunTask with both task and taskFile rejects with a NaxError whose code is AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and whose message is pass exactly one of --task or --task-file.
[unit] resolveAgentsRunTask({ taskFile: "task.md", cwd: "/repo", catalog }, { readText }) calls readText with /repo/task.md and resolves to the text readText returns.
[unit] resolveAgentsRunTask({ taskFile: "/abs/task.md", cwd: "/repo", catalog }, { readText }) calls readText with /abs/task.md.

[unit] when readText rejects with an error whose message is ENOENT, resolveAgentsRunTask rejects with a NaxError whose code is AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and whose message is cannot read task file task.md: ENOENT.
[unit] with the default reader, resolveAgentsRunTask({ taskFile: "task.md", cwd: <temp dir>, catalog }) resolves to the text of a task.md written in that temp directory.
[unit] resolveAgentsRunTask({ task: "   ", cwd, catalog }) rejects with a NaxError whose code is AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and whose message is the task is empty.

[unit] with a catalog whose findSkill("spec-review") returns a skill, resolveAgentsRunTask({ task: "/spec-review .nax/features/x/spec.md", cwd, catalog }) resolves to exactly buildSkillInvocationMessage({ skill, args: ".nax/features/x/spec.md" }).
[unit] with a catalog whose findSkill("nax-spec-kit:spec-review") returns a skill, a task /nax-spec-kit:spec-review with no arguments resolves to buildSkillInvocationMessage({ skill, args: "" }).
[unit] a task "  /spec-review   a.md  " calls findSkill with spec-review and resolves to the message built with args "a.md".
[unit] with a catalog whose findSkill returns undefined, a task /nope a.md rejects with a NaxError whose code is AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and whose message is skill nope not found.
[unit] a task review /spec-review a.md (the slash is not first) resolves to the text unchanged and findSkill is never called.
[unit] a task / alone resolves to / unchanged and findSkill is never called.

routing.reasoning: Bounded task parsing and injected file reading reuse existing catalog and prompt-builder contracts.

suggestedCriteria: When task is "  review the spec  ", resolveAgentsRunTask returns the original surrounding whitespace unchanged.
When task is "/spec-review! a.md", resolveAgentsRunTask returns it unchanged without calling findSkill.
When a task file contains only whitespace, resolveAgentsRunTask rejects with AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and message the task is empty.

userStories.title: Unattended asks, timeout and cancellation
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Deny unattended asks immediately and implement deterministic cancellation and timeout precedence.

**Motivation** — `nax run` and `nax plan` exit 0 on failure, which is why a new command must not.

**Approach** — The command runs the agent in mode `guarded` and attaches no interaction chain. It answers every ask itself, the moment it arrives, through the nested session's `answer`:

- An `approval_requested` event that is answerable (its `answerable` is not `false`) is answered `{ decision: "deny" }` and recorded as `{ kind: "approval", tool, summary }`.
- A `question` event that is answerable is answered `{ text: AGENTS_RUN_NO_ANSWER }` and recorded as `{ kind: "question", text }`, where `AGENTS_RUN_NO_ANSWER = "No one is attached to answer. Continue without an answer, or stop and say what you need."`.
- An event with `answerable: false` was already decided by the session's profile; it is not answered and not recorded.
- Every answerable ask is recorded whatever `answer` returns (`accepted`, `expired`, `cancelled` or `unknown`). If `answer` throws, the error is caught and the ask is still recorded; the run goes on. `runSubagent` calls `onSession` before the turn's first event, so an ask always has a session to answer it on.

The turn continues after a denial. Ask handling is not what keeps an unattended agent from writing; the tool set and profile are:

- **ACP models:** the profile (next section). An agent with no `tools:` line, or one that declares only non-write tools, opens on the read-only `review` profile.
- **Native models:** a native subagent session always opens with profile `full` (`chatSessionSettings`, `packages/nax/src/chat/chat-mode.ts`), and `resolveTuiPermissions` defaults `askRules` to `[]`, so a write inside the workdir would raise no ask. So for a native model whose agent file has no `tools:` line, the command narrows the tools to `AGENTS_RUN_NATIVE_READ_TOOLS = ["Read", "Glob", "Grep", "Git", "nax-skills__*", "nax-workflow__*"]` (`Git` is the native read-only git tool). An agent file that declares `tools:` gets `mapSubagentTools(agent.tools).allowedTools`; if those include a write tool, the agent can write, and the configured `execution.permissions` ask and deny rules (whose asks are denied) are the only guard.

The native tool narrowing is composed in US-007; profile derivation belongs to US-001.

`--timeout <seconds>` is a positive whole number: the text must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`. With no `--timeout` there is no command-level limit; the session's own default turn limit (`DEFAULT_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 3600 s, in `packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-options.ts`) still applies and ends the turn `timed_out`, which maps to status `timeout`. The same limit caps a `--timeout` above 3600: the turn ends at 3600 s with status `timeout`. Raising the session limit is out of scope. Raw timeout validation belongs to US-008; runAgentTask receives timeoutSeconds.

**Status mapping.** The run's status comes from these rules, in order:

1. The command's own `--timeout` timer fired: `timeout`, whatever the turn then reported (even `completed`) and even when a signal also arrived.
2. A SIGINT or SIGTERM arrived: `cancelled`, whatever the turn then reported (even `completed`), and also when `runSubagent` returned without any `turn_end` because the signal stopped it before the turn began. The signal handlers stay registered until the run resolves; a second signal aborts an already aborted controller and changes nothing.
3. A `turn_end` event arrived: `completed` -> `completed`, `cancelled` -> `cancelled`, `timed_out` -> `timeout`, `errored` -> `failed`, `interrupted` -> `failed`.
4. No `turn_end` arrived (the session refused to start, or session creation failed): `failed`.

Extend runAgentTask, keeping the US-003 result and propagation contract. Link input.signal to an internal AbortController, support an already-aborted input, and arm only an explicit timeout. Clear the timer and unlink the signal in finally. `_agentsRunExecDeps = { runSubagent, setTimeout, clearTimeout }` (a cancellable timer, so `setTimeout` is the permitted exception; the call site says so). Use makeFakeClock, not real waits. Its tests go in their own file, `agents-run-exec-asks.test.ts`, split by concern from `agents-run-exec.test.ts` because the two story sets together would pass the 650-line test-file target.

**Scope** — In: immediate ask replies, ordered recording, reply-error tolerance, timer and abort linkage, status override and cleanup. Out: native/ACP tool composition (US-001/007), OS signal registration (US-009), timeout text parsing (US-008), output formatting (US-005). No interaction chain (Telegram, webhook) is attached, so no ask is ever forwarded to a person. Raising the session's 3600 s turn limit; a `--timeout` above it is capped by it.

**Interface** —
```typescript
runAgentTask(input: AgentsRunTaskInput, deps?: typeof _agentsRunExecDeps): Promise<AgentsRunResult>
```
`AGENTS_RUN_NO_ANSWER = "No one is attached to answer. Continue without an answer, or stop and say what you need."`; `AgentSession.answer(requestId: string, reply: AnswerReply): AnswerStatus` is consumed unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] when the stubbed runSubagent calls onSession with a fake session and then emits an answerable approval_requested with requestId r1, tool Bash and summary rm -rf build, the fake session's answer is called once with ("r1", { decision: "deny" }).

userStories.title: Output and exit code for a run result
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Provide a pure formatter for plain/JSON results and completed-versus-failed exit codes.

**Motivation** — `nax run` and `nax plan` exit 0 on failure, which is why a new command must not.

**Approach** — Without `--json`, a completed turn prints its final text to stdout followed by a newline; any other outcome prints the result text to stderr. In plain mode each denied ask is also written to stderr, after the result text, one line each, in arrival order: `[agents run] denied <tool>: <summary>` for an approval and `[agents run] unanswered question: <text>` for a question. With `--json`, the command prints exactly one JSON object and a newline to stdout for every outcome in which the agent ran or tried to start:
```json
{
  "agent": "superpowers:code-reviewer",
  "model": "acp:codex/gpt-6.1-terra",
  "status": "completed",
  "output": "VERDICT: ready\n...",
  "deniedAsks": [
    { "kind": "approval", "tool": "Bash", "summary": "rm -rf build" },
    { "kind": "question", "text": "Which file should I review?" }
  ],
  "costUsd": 0.42
}
```

`agent` is the agent's `qualifiedName`; `model` is the resolved model string. `status` is one of `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled`, `timeout`. `output` is the text `runSubagent` returned: the final text on completion, the error text otherwise. `costUsd` is present only when the turn ended with a `turn_end` event whose `costSource` is not `unpriced`; an unpriced turn (an ACP agent that reported no cost) and a run that never reached a turn both omit it. It is never written as `0` to mean unknown.

A usage or config error (exit 2) prints a one-line message to stderr and no JSON, in both modes. The command waits until stdout and stderr have accepted every write before it exits, so a long reviewer output piped to a file is never cut short. A completed turn with no text has the output `(the subagent returned no text)`, the placeholder `runSubagent` already returns; it is still status `completed`, exit 0. Command writes and pre-result errors are owned by US-008/009; this module writes nothing.

**Writers.** `writeOut(text)` and `writeErr(text)` write `text` exactly as given, adding nothing, and return a promise that resolves once the stream has accepted it. Every one-line error message is written as `${message}\n`; `agentsRunOutput`'s strings already end in a newline and are written unchanged.

Exit 0 for status completed; exit 1 for failed, cancelled or timeout. JSON mode has no stderr; serialize the result directly so absent costUsd stays absent and embedded newlines/quotes are escaped into one physical JSON line.

**Scope** — In: pure stream strings and exitCode for a run result. Out: terminal-event/cost derivation (US-003), ask handling (US-004), command usage/config error formatting and asynchronous writes (US-008/009). The command does not interpret the agent's output or extract a verdict; a caller asks for one in the task text and parses it.

**Interface** —
```typescript
agentsRunOutput(result: AgentsRunResult, json: boolean): AgentsRunOutput

interface AgentsRunOutput { readonly stdout?: string; readonly stderr?: string; readonly exitCode: 0 | 1 }
```
Pure: it decides what to print and the exit code; it writes nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] agentsRunOutput(result, false) for a result with status completed, output VERDICT: ready and no denied asks returns a value deep-equal to { stdout: "VERDICT: ready\n", exitCode: 0 }.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, false) for a result with status failed, output boom and no denied asks returns a value deep-equal to { stderr: "boom\n", exitCode: 1 }.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, false) for status cancelled and output c returns a value deep-equal to { stderr: "c\n", exitCode: 1 }.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, false) for status timeout and output t returns a value deep-equal to { stderr: "t\n", exitCode: 1 }.

[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, false) for a completed result whose deniedAsks is [{ kind: "approval", tool: "Bash", summary: "rm x" }, { kind: "question", text: "Which?" }] returns stderr equal to [agents run] denied Bash: rm x\n[agents run] unanswered question: Which?\n.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, false) for a failed result with output boom and one denied approval Bash / rm x returns stderr equal to boom\n[agents run] denied Bash: rm x\n.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, true) for a completed result returns exitCode 0, no stderr, and a stdout that is one line ending in a newline whose JSON parse deep-equals the result object.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, true) for a result with status failed returns exitCode 1, no stderr, and a stdout whose JSON parse has status failed.
[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, true) for a result with no costUsd returns JSON with no costUsd key.

[unit] agentsRunOutput(result, true) for a result whose output contains a newline and a double quote returns a stdout with exactly one newline, at the end, whose JSON parse restores the output exactly.

routing.reasoning: Pure formatting and exit-code mapping have no I/O, session control or new dependencies.

userStories.title: Resolve the run's model
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve the selected agent model lazily while rejecting unknown explicit overrides.

**Motivation** — koda's runner can launch `nax plan`, `nax run`, `nax bot review` and `nax bot fix`, but it cannot run "the spec reviewer on this spec" as a job, and the koda flow needs exactly that.

**Approach** — **Model** (`resolveAgentsRunModel`): `resolveSubagentModel({ requested, parentModel, aliases, tiers })` where `requested` is `--model` when given and otherwise the agent's `model`, `aliases` is `config.agent.modelAliases ?? {}` and `tiers` is `config.models.native`. `parentModel` is `models.native.balanced` written as a `provider/model` string (an entry is either that string or `{ provider, model }`), or the empty string when it is unset. The parent model is needed **lazily**: after resolution,
1. `--model` given and source `fallback`: usage error `unknown model <id>; ...` (this wins even when `models.native.balanced` is unset);

userStories.title: The command's checks and errors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add directly callable command orchestration with ordered validation, noninteractive trust and exact exit-2 errors.

**Motivation** — `nax run` and `nax plan` exit 0 on failure, which is why a new command must not.

**Approach** — **Check order.** The command checks, in this order, and stops at the first failure: the `--timeout` text; trust; config; the catalog and the agent; the task (`resolveAgentsRunTask`); the model (`resolveAgentsRunModel`). Trust comes before anything that reads repository-controlled content, so an untrusted project never has its config or catalog loaded.

`--timeout <seconds>` is a positive whole number: the text must match `^[1-9][0-9]*$`. With no `--timeout` there is no command-level limit; the session's own default turn limit (`DEFAULT_TURN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, 3600 s, in `packages/nax-agent/src/session/agent-session-options.ts`) still applies and ends the turn `timed_out`, which maps to status `timeout`. The same limit caps a `--timeout` above 3600: the turn ends at 3600 s with status `timeout`. Raising the session limit is out of scope.

`-d, --dir <path>` is the working directory. It is the **parent** `agents` command's existing option (`bin/nax.ts`, default `process.cwd()` at the CLI boundary): commander gives a parent's known option to the parent even when it follows the subcommand name, so `run` declares no `-d` of its own and reads the directory with `command.optsWithGlobals().dir`. `nax agents run x -d /d --task t` therefore runs in `/d`. The command resolves it to an absolute path with `resolve(dir)` before any use, so `cwd`, the trust root and relative `--task-file` paths are all absolute. Registration belongs to US-009.

`--profile` is repeatable; each value may be comma-separated. The raw values are collected in order and passed to `loadConfig(naxDir ?? undefined, { profile: values })` only when at least one was given, and `loadConfig(naxDir ?? undefined)` otherwise, as `composeChat` does; `loadConfig` splits the comma lists itself.

`<agent>` is looked up with `ResourceCatalog.findAgent`, so a short name (`spec-reviewer`) or a qualified name (`superpowers:code-reviewer`) both work. **Catalog:** `loadResourceCatalog({ repoRoot, config, env, naxPluginPackages: [] })`. The repo root is `dirname(findProjectDir(cwd))` when a `.nax` directory is found, and `cwd` otherwise, as in `nax chat`.

`packages/nax/src/cli/agents-run.ts`: `agentsRunCommand(agent: string, options: AgentsRunOptions, deps?: AgentsRunCommandDeps): Promise<void>` and `registerAgentsRunCommand(agents: Command, deps?: AgentsRunCommandDeps): Command`, with the interfaces below. US-009 adds registerAgentsRunCommand, production registration and both command barrel exports; references below to registration and exports describe the final combined target rather than additional US-008 work.

`_agentsRunCommandDeps` holds `ensureTrusted`, `loadConfig`, `findProjectDir`, `loadResourceCatalog`, `resolveAgentsRunTask`, `buildAgentsRunTaskInput`, `runAgentTask`, `env`, `writeOut`, `writeErr`, `setExitCode`, `onSignal`, `exit`, following `_chatCommandDeps` in `packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts`. `writeOut` and `writeErr` follow "Writers" above. The default `ensureTrusted(cwd)` calls `ensureProjectTrusted(await normalizeTrustPath(resolveTrustRoot(cwd)), { interactive: false })`. The registered action awaits `agentsRunCommand` and then calls `deps.exit()`, as `registerChatCommand` does. Both functions are exported from `packages/nax/src/cli/index.ts`.

**Writers.** `writeOut(text)` and `writeErr(text)` write `text` exactly as given, adding nothing, and return a promise that resolves once the stream has accepted it. Every one-line error message is written as `${message}\n`; `agentsRunOutput`'s strings already end in a newline and are written unchanged.

A usage or config error (exit 2) prints a one-line message to stderr and no JSON, in both modes. Special untrusted-project handling prints `Project not trusted: <root>` then the error's hint line (or `run: nax trust add <root>`). Trust errors for another reason, config/catalog failures, and any other error thrown before a run result exists use the error message and exit 2. Unknown agent uses `agent <name> not found; see nax agents`. Task and model helpers' AGENTS_RUN_USAGE messages propagate unchanged with a newline. Neither/both task flags use `pass exactly one of --task or --task-file`; unreadable task uses `cannot read task file <path>: <reason>`; empty task uses `the task is empty`; unknown skill uses `skill <name> not found`; bad timeout uses `--timeout must be a positive whole number of seconds`; invalid explicit model uses `unknown model <id>; pass provider/model, acp:<agent>, or a configured alias`; missing balanced fallback uses `configure models.native.balanced or pass --model`.

US-008 consumes `resolveAgentsRunTask` (US-002) and `buildAgentsRunTaskInput` (US-007): its tests call `agentsRunCommand` with stubbed deps and assert the arguments they receive and what is written to stderr. Build sufficient executable orchestration to expose composition arguments on valid calls, then US-009 completes result output, signal lifecycle and registration. Do not import the US-005 output module before that dependency is available.

**Scope** — In: absolute cwd, timeout text validation, trust, config/catalog/agent lookup, ordered task/model delegation, command dependency seam, pre-result errors and awaited usage-error writes. Out: final run-result formatting and signal/registration/explicit-exit lifecycle (US-009), task/model algorithms (US-002/006). `nax agents run` loads no nax plugins and no agent hooks, attaches no memory host or memory tools, connects no catalog MCP servers and offers no `nax-jobs` launch tools; nax-plugin-provided agents and skills are therefore not found by it. Checking that `--dir` exists before the trust check; a missing directory fails at the trust check or config load as an exit-2 error.

**Interface** —
```typescript
export interface AgentsRunOptions {
  readonly dir: string; // from the parent agents command, via optsWithGlobals
  readonly task?: string;
  readonly taskFile?: string;
  readonly profile?: readonly string[]; // raw repeated values; loadConfig splits commas
  readonly model?: string;
  readonly json?: boolean;
  readonly timeout?: string; // raw text, validated by the command
}
export type AgentsRunCommandDeps = typeof _agentsRunCommandDeps;
```
```typescript
agentsRunCommand(agent: string, options: AgentsRunOptions, deps?: AgentsRunCommandDeps): Promise<void>
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] agentsRunCommand("a", { dir: "sub", task: "t" }, deps) calls the stubbed ensureTrusted with the absolute path resolve("sub").
[unit] that call passes cwd equal to resolve("sub") to the stubbed buildAgentsRunTaskInput.
[unit] repoRoot passed to buildAgentsRunTaskInput is the parent of the directory the stubbed findProjectDir returns, and is the resolved dir when findProjectDir returns null.

[unit] for each timeout value in the table 0, -3, 1.5, abc, 45abc, 1e2, the command calls writeErr with --timeout must be a positive whole number of seconds\n, sets exit code 2, and never calls ensureTrusted.
[unit] timeout "45" makes buildAgentsRunTaskInput receive timeoutSeconds 45.

[unit] when ensureTrusted throws a NaxError with code PROJECT_UNTRUSTED and context { root: "/r", hint: "run: nax trust add /r" }, writeErr is called with Project not trusted: /r\n and then run: nax trust add /r\n, and the exit code is 2.
[unit] in that untrusted case, neither loadConfig nor loadResourceCatalog is called.
[unit] when ensureTrusted throws a NaxError with code TRUST_STORE_UNREADABLE and message trust store unreadable, writeErr is called with trust store unreadable\n and the exit code is 2.
[unit] after useUntrustedRegistry(), the default _agentsRunCommandDeps.ensureTrusted on a temp directory rejects with a NaxError code PROJECT_UNTRUSTED and never calls _trustGateDeps.prompt.
[unit] with profile: ["a,b", "c"] and findProjectDir returning /repo/.nax, loadConfig is called with ("/repo/.nax", { profile: ["a,b", "c"] }).
[unit] with no profile and findProjectDir returning null, loadConfig is called with exactly one argument, undefined.
[unit] loadResourceCatalog receives an argument deep-equal to { repoRoot, config, env: deps.env, naxPluginPackages: [] }.
[unit] when loadConfig rejects with an error whose message is bad config, writeErr is called with bad config\n and the exit code is 2.
[unit] when loadResourceCatalog rejects with an error whose message is catalog broke, writeErr is called with catalog broke\n and the exit code is 2.
[unit] when the catalog's findAgent returns undefined for ghost, writeErr is called with agent ghost not found; see nax agents\n, the exit code is 2, and resolveAgentsRunTask is never called.
[unit] with json: true and an unknown agent ghost, writeOut is never called.

[unit] when resolveAgentsRunTask rejects with a NaxError code AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and message skill nope not found, writeErr is called with skill nope not found\n, the exit code is 2, and buildAgentsRunTaskInput is never called.

[unit] when buildAgentsRunTaskInput throws a NaxError code AGENTS_RUN_USAGE with message configure models.native.balanced or pass --model, writeErr is called with that message and a newline, and the exit code is 2.

[unit] when resolveAgentsRunTask rejects with AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and message pass exactly one of --task or --task-file for either missing or conflicting task sources, agentsRunCommand writes that message followed by a newline to stderr as an exit-2 response without stdout, in both plain and json modes.

[unit] when resolveAgentsRunTask rejects with AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and message cannot read task file task.md: ENOENT, agentsRunCommand writes that message followed by a newline to stderr as an exit-2 response without stdout, in both plain and json modes.

[unit] when resolveAgentsRunTask rejects with AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and message the task is empty, agentsRunCommand writes that message followed by a newline to stderr as an exit-2 response without stdout, in both plain and json modes.

[unit] when buildAgentsRunTaskInput throws AGENTS_RUN_USAGE and message unknown model nonsense; pass provider/model, acp:<agent>, or a configured alias, agentsRunCommand writes that message followed by a newline to stderr as an exit-2 response without stdout, in both plain and json modes.

routing.reasoning: One command module follows composeChat and its injected dependencies without a new abstraction; strict security TDD is required because trust must precede repository-controlled config and catalog reads.

suggestedCriteria: When timeout is "01", "+1", " 1" or "1 ", agentsRunCommand emits --timeout must be a positive whole number of seconds followed by a newline before any trust check.
When profile is [], loadConfig receives only naxDir ?? undefined and no override argument.
When PROJECT_UNTRUSTED has no hint, agentsRunCommand prints run: nax trust add <root> as the second stderr line.
When ensureTrusted rejects with a generic error other than PROJECT_UNTRUSTED, agentsRunCommand reports its message with exit code 2.

When timeout text is valid and all checks succeed, recorded dependency calls occur in order ensureTrusted, findProjectDir, loadConfig, loadResourceCatalog, catalog.findAgent, resolveAgentsRunTask, buildAgentsRunTaskInput.

userStories.title: Run, output, signals and registration
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Complete command execution and expose the production agents run subcommand with drained output and deterministic signal cleanup.

**Motivation** — `nax run` and `nax plan` exit 0 on failure, which is why a new command must not.

**Approach** —
```text
nax agents run <agent> (--task <text> | --task-file <path>)
              [-d, --dir <path>] [--profile <names>] [--model <id>] [--json] [--timeout <seconds>]
```

`<agent>` is looked up with `ResourceCatalog.findAgent`, so a short name (`spec-reviewer`) or a qualified name (`superpowers:code-reviewer`) both work. Exactly one of `--task` and `--task-file` is required. `--task-file` is read as UTF-8 text with `Bun.file(path).text()`; a relative path resolves against `--dir`. The command's ordered checks and helpers are already supplied by US-008/002/006/007; registration must preserve that ordering rather than using a pre-trust commander task-option check.

`--profile` is repeatable; each value may be comma-separated. The raw values are collected in order and passed to `loadConfig(naxDir ?? undefined, { profile: values })` only when at least one was given, and `loadConfig(naxDir ?? undefined)` otherwise, as `composeChat` does; `loadConfig` splits the comma lists itself. `--model <id>` takes the place of the agent file's `model:` value in model resolution.

`-d, --dir <path>` is the working directory. It is the **parent** `agents` command's existing option (`bin/nax.ts`, default `process.cwd()` at the CLI boundary): commander gives a parent's known option to the parent even when it follows the subcommand name, so `run` declares no `-d` of its own and reads the directory with `command.optsWithGlobals().dir`. `nax agents run x -d /d --task t` therefore runs in `/d`. The command resolves it to an absolute path with `resolve(dir)` before any use, so `cwd`, the trust root and relative `--task-file` paths are all absolute. The bare `nax agents` command keeps listing coding agents, unchanged. `run` is added as its subcommand.

The `agents` command in `packages/nax/bin/nax.ts`. Target: the `Command` returned by `program.command("agents")...` (which keeps its `-d, --dir` option and listing action) is passed to `registerAgentsRunCommand`, which adds the `run` subcommand.

`_agentsRunCommandDeps` holds `ensureTrusted`, `loadConfig`, `findProjectDir`, `loadResourceCatalog`, `resolveAgentsRunTask`, `buildAgentsRunTaskInput`, `runAgentTask`, `env`, `writeOut`, `writeErr`, `setExitCode`, `onSignal`, `exit`, following `_chatCommandDeps` in `packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts`. `writeOut` and `writeErr` follow "Writers" above. The default `ensureTrusted(cwd)` calls `ensureProjectTrusted(await normalizeTrustPath(resolveTrustRoot(cwd)), { interactive: false })`. The registered action awaits `agentsRunCommand` and then calls `deps.exit()`, as `registerChatCommand` does. Both functions are exported from `packages/nax/src/cli/index.ts`.

**Writers.** `writeOut(text)` and `writeErr(text)` write `text` exactly as given, adding nothing, and return a promise that resolves once the stream has accepted it. Every one-line error message is written as `${message}\n`; `agentsRunOutput`'s strings already end in a newline and are written unchanged.

**Output.** Without `--json`, a completed turn prints its final text to stdout followed by a newline; any other outcome prints the result text to stderr. In plain mode each denied ask is also written to stderr, after the result text, one line each, in arrival order: `[agents run] denied <tool>: <summary>` for an approval and `[agents run] unanswered question: <text>` for a question. With `--json`, the command prints exactly one JSON object and a newline to stdout for every outcome in which the agent ran or tried to start. Delegate these decisions to agentsRunOutput and write its strings unchanged; never stream event deltas or add a second newline. A usage or config error (exit 2) prints a one-line message to stderr and no JSON, in both modes. The command waits until stdout and stderr have accepted every write before it exits, so a long reviewer output piped to a file is never cut short.

**Exit codes.** 0: status `completed`. 1: status `failed`, `cancelled` or `timeout`. 2: a usage or config error: bad options, untrusted project, config that fails to load, agent or skill not found, a model that cannot be resolved, a native session whose options cannot be built, or any other error thrown before a run result exists. A runAgentTask rejection prints the error message and newline with exit 2, no JSON. A returned failed refusal is an ordinary result with exit 1. Preserve parser usage errors as exit 2.

A SIGINT or SIGTERM arrived: `cancelled`, whatever the turn then reported (even `completed`), and also when `runSubagent` returned without any `turn_end` because the signal stopped it before the turn began. The signal handlers stay registered until the run resolves; a second signal aborts an already aborted controller and changes nothing. The command's own `--timeout` timer fired: `timeout`, whatever the turn then reported (even `completed`) and even when a signal also arrived. US-004 owns the priority mapping; this story registers both signals and supplies the same command-owned abort signal to runAgentTask, replacing any signal in the composed input. Remove all registered handlers on run settlement, including failure.

US-009 consumes `runAgentTask` (US-003, US-004) and `agentsRunOutput` (US-005): its tests enter through a commander program whose `agents` command (with `-d, --dir`) was passed to `registerAgentsRunCommand`, parse an argv, and assert what reaches `runAgentTask` and what is written; the last AC spawns `bin/nax.ts` to prove the production registration. Its last AC spawns `bun bin/nax.ts agents run --help`; that is the story-required smoke exception to the no-full-CLI-spawn rule, as `test/unit/cli/chat.test.ts` AC-18 is for `nax chat`, and help opens no session.

**Scope** — In: runAgentTask integration, output delegation, awaited writers, signals/cleanup, commander options/action, barrel exports and bin registration. Out: helper algorithms and profile derivation (US-001 through US-008). Changing the `nax agents` listing output. No chat tool or chat card launches `nax agents run`; the chat brain never starts it. Section 4 of the design (`nax-flow__send`, koda credentials, sending a flow to koda) is a later feature. The command does not interpret the agent's output or extract a verdict; a caller asks for one in the task text and parses it. No resume: every run opens a fresh memory-only session and closes it after one turn. Updating `docs/guides/cli-reference.md` for `nax agents run`; it is a docs follow-up after merge.

**Interface** —
```typescript
agentsRunCommand(agent: string, options: AgentsRunOptions, deps?: AgentsRunCommandDeps): Promise<void>
registerAgentsRunCommand(agents: Command, deps?: AgentsRunCommandDeps): Command
```
Use AgentsRunOptions and AgentsRunCommandDeps from US-008. Export agentsRunCommand and registerAgentsRunCommand from packages/nax/src/cli/index.ts.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] when agentsRunCommand runs with stubbed deps, the stubbed runAgentTask is called once with the input the stubbed buildAgentsRunTaskInput returned, with its signal replaced by the command's own abort signal.

routing.reasoning: Command, bin and barrel wiring reuse registerChatCommand, the completed executor and formatter; signal cleanup and awaited writers are standard lifecycle work, but session launch requires strict security TDD.

analysis:
Repository exploration: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this session, so findings were established with direct source reads and targeted searches. This is an additive enhancement to the existing Bun/TypeScript CLI, not a new agent runtime. All nine stories work in packages/nax; packages/nax-agent, packages/nax-agent-acp and packages/nax-ai are read-only dependencies for this feature. No dependency, manifest, release, persistence-format or public npm API migration is required. The binding story IDs, workdirs and dependency edges must remain unchanged.

Architecture and existing lifecycle: packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-session.ts:29 defines RunSubagentInput and :55 defines RunSubagentResult; :61 exposes the injectable _subagentSessionDeps seam. Native options are constructed before session creation (:70), with guarded posture resolved through resolveTuiPermissions (:250), a memory-only transcript (:102), rules-index instructions (:105), optional allowedTools (:92), loopHandlers and subagent role (:89). runSubagent (:240) already selects native versus ACP by the model, checks an already-aborted signal, and returns error results for model parsing, session creation and ACP option-building failures. Native option construction is deliberately outside the session-creation catch (:251), so it can reject and must become command exit 2, not a fabricated failed run result. driveTurn (:145) forwards every event in order and derives the returned content from turn_end; resultOfTurn (:136) already supplies '(the subagent returned no text)' for a completed empty output. runOnSession (:162) calls onSession before driveTurn, links cancellation, removes its abort listener and closes the session in finally. closeQuietly (:151) logs close failure without replacing the result. Reuse all of this; do not open or close a second session, stream provisional deltas as final output, or reinterpret isError as the sole terminal-status authority. No turn_end with a returned refusal/creation error means failed; a rejected runSubagent means there is no run result and command exit 2.

Existing ACP behavior and dependents: packages/nax/src/chat/acp/acp-subagent-profile.ts:23 defines exactly six write-tool names; :50 currently applies override, then missing tools or write tools inherit chat posture, otherwise review. Add optional unattended?: true so only the missing-tools unattended branch changes; preserve existing tool bare-name handling, Bash classification, override precedence and read-only-enforcement capability lookup (:71). packages/nax/src/chat/subagent-session.ts:179 derives the ACP profile and :192 refuses review/read on clients without their own read-only enforcement, including cursor. outOfScope: `nax agents run` loads no nax plugins and no agent hooks, attaches no memory host or memory tools, connects no catalog MCP servers and offers no `nax-jobs` launch tools; nax-plugin-provided agents and skills are therefore not found by it.
Catalog commands (`findCommand` templates, including their `` !`cmd` `` shell lines) are not expanded in `--task`; only skills are.
No chat tool or chat card launches `nax agents run`; the chat brain never starts it.
The command does not interpret the agent's output or extract a verdict; a caller asks for one in the task text and parses it.
Section 4 of the design (`nax-flow__send`, koda credentials, sending a flow to koda) is a later feature.
No interaction chain (Telegram, webhook) is attached, so no ask is ever forwarded to a person.
No resume: every run opens a fresh memory-only session and closes it after one turn.
Translating an agent file's `tools:` list into ACP tool restrictions beyond read-only versus not is unchanged from part (a).
Enforcing read-only for a native agent whose `tools:` line declares a write tool: such an agent can write, and the configured `execution.permissions` rules are its only guard.
